newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW says 7-month group sales up 9.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: VW says 7-month group sales up 9.5 percent.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday that its deliveries to customers for the first seven months of 1997 rose 9.5 percent to 2.525 million vehicles.
VW also said at the presentation of the new Golf model that Volkswagen brand vehicle deliveries during the period from January to July rose 6.4 percent to 1.6 million units.
VW sells vehicles under the Volkswagen, Audi, SEAT and Skoda brands.
VW management board member Robert Buechelhofer told a news conference that Volkswagen brand sales growth occurred in particular in South America and Asia.
He said sales in western Europe were mostly flat at 880,000 vehicles during the period.
For the global vehicle market in 1997, Buechelhofer said VW expected growth of about 1.6 percent to 37 million vehicles.
Buechelhofer said VW, the world's fourth-largest car maker, would seek to maintain its global market share of about 10 percent.
